title: Search Index Lifecycle
readerIntent: Design and operate index creation, synchronization, evolution, reconciliation, and retirement.
priorKnowledge: Understand authoritative schemas and derived search indexes.
owner: Owning business capability, nSearch, and configured provider
summary: Indexes are derived projections whose mappings, documents, aliases, and lifecycle must remain reconcilable with authoritative records.

sections.heading: Lifecycle stages
items: Define index ownership, identity, fields, tenant routing, and refresh policy.
Create mapping and index or alias structures.
Populate initial records in bounded batches.
Apply incremental create, update, and delete changes.
Detect indexing lag, missing documents, duplicates, and mapping conflicts.
Reindex into a new version when incompatible mappings change.
Retire old indexes through a governed cleanup and rollback window.

sections.heading: Failure behavior
paragraphs: A successful database mutation and a failed index mutation must remain observable and reconcilable. Do not report the search projection as authoritative or silently discard partial bulk failures.

sections.heading: Schema evolution
items: Classify compatible versus incompatible field changes.
Version mappings and aliases when in-place updates are unsafe.
Test old and new query behavior before cutover.
Preserve tenant isolation and rollback evidence throughout migration.
